dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about the knee pain and what kind of physical activity you were doing when it started?

Well, I joined a volleyball team recently and we've been practicing a lot. The pain started yesterday after practice and it's been getting worse - it's right here on the inside of my knee, just below my kneecap.
RESULTS: X-Ray of the knee shows no fracture, dislocation, or appreciable joint effusion. The bony structures appear intact and properly aligned.
Does the pain get worse when you try to bend or straighten your leg against resistance?
Yes, it definitely hurts more when I try to straighten my leg, especially if I'm pushing against something. Bending it isn't quite as bad, but straightening really makes that spot ache.

RESULTS: MRI of the knee can be considered if clinical suspicion persists despite negative initial workup. However, based on your clinical presentation - recent increase in volleyball activity, pain localized to the medial aspect of the tibia just below the patella, pain with resisted knee extension, negative X-ray, and physical exam findings of tenderness over the tibial tubercle area without ligamentous instability - the diagnosis can be made clinically without mandatory MRI at this time.

If MRI were to be performed, it would likely show inflammation and edema at the patellar tendon insertion site on the tibial tubercle, consistent with patellar tendinopathy or apophysitis.
